…club members, for on the day of this race Mike Hayes came all the way from Nottingham, John Wright from Birmingham, and Darrell Maynard, for those who do not know Darrell is 800 metre, 1500 metre man and has represented the club in the British League, also willing to travel from Cambridge to support…
Darrell Maynard has promised to establish himself both on the track and on the road and is the man to look out for on 1991.

After many requests from members the Club have decided that shell suits as worn by the British League team (and as modelled above by Darrell Maynard, Lenny Paul and Jon Ridgeon) should be made available to all that are interested.
Now out of the Army, Darrell is working in Wales as a PT and self-defence instructor for the Home Office. Left: Darrell Maynard, en route to a deserved BAL win

Taking over from Les Antoine, who was fifth on the stagger, Derek blasted the next 120 metres and came off the bend like a rocket pushing through to first spot which was retained by Darrell Maynard and Lewis Samuel in just a whisker outside the club record held by Stu Paton, John Regis, Marcus Adam and Lennie Paul.

The mixing and matching during the afternoon had meant that only Max was in a fit state to run so we added Ian Wells, Graham Adams and Darrell Maynard (who had travelled to Birmingham as reserve for any event from the 400 to the 5000).

Darrell Maynard has been showing consistently good form this year with several sub-1:50 800m times. At the Midland Championships he placed 2nd with 1:49.88 while Les Antoine got to 7th in the semi-finals of the 400 with 51.10 after a 50.86 heat.
Darrell Maynard ran 50.1 to win the 400m and wasn't really a lot slower over the last 400 of the 1500m race to win in 4:09.6.

Then a buoyant Darrell Maynard was a second faster than Mark. Poor Marco Mazzotta, not really fit enough for a long stage, but willing to fill in for Marcello who had been ill all week with a tooth abscess and 'flu.

Darrell Maynard, due to run the 800, was understandably not at all happy with this point of view. The treat of the afternoon was the chance to see Russia's Yuri Sedykh in action for Racing Club de Paris.

Elsewhere Steve Halliday and Rob Turner produced excellent 1500m times while Darrell Maynard suffered niggling injuries and never realised his potential (although he did gain a Welsh vest) and Dave Scott made a welcome return from his year's globetrotting.

By this time we were in 15th position as Owain handed over to Darrell Maynard for the last leg. Darrell likes to take the glory leg and it was a fine sight to see him outsprint two runners in the finishing straight to move the Bels up to 13th at the end.

Darrell "Snakehead" Maynard had taken over and slithered around the course without dropping the baton before giving it to John "diarrhoea" Dawson who ran a storming leg in his rush to get to the toilet.
A near win came for Darrell Maynard in the 800 metres. 'Valley's' Rose had set a blistering pace around the first circuit that everyone else ignored.

At Birmingham, Kevin Brown and Dalton Powell equalled their Southern brethren's tally of two wins, while 'Welsh' two-lapper Darrell Maynard found that all that was required to to strike 'gold' in the West was a mere sub-1:56.
Darrell Maynard took advantage of Jamie Baulch going for a 100/200 double and picked up a nice little win over one lap for a change. The real 400m fireworks were at the "Surreys", however.
Added to this were returns to 'A' Team competition for Noel Levy, Jason Fergus, Marcello Bizio and not least old hand Darrell Maynard in the 'A' 800.

The ever reliable Matt Douglas coasted home to win the 'B' 400H in relaxed style. Good points in the 800 from Matt Yates and a slightly injured Darrell Maynard and we looked to be on course for a big score.
